title: Direct Observation Of Switching Anion Filament In Phase-Separated 2D Halide (PbI2)x(BiI3)1-x Memristor
content: As traditional devices encounter physical limitations, memristors are being explored as promising breakthroughs for next-generation neuromorphic computing and memory applications. The memristors exhibit voltage-driven modulation of memresistance (M) with nonlinear bipolar I-V hysteresis [1-2]. Their ability to reversibly switch between a high resistive state (HRS) and a low resistive state (LRS) allows binary data storage, representing 0 and 1. This memristive behavior has been identified in 2D metal chalcogenide semiconductors such as MoS2, TaS2, WS2, MoSe2, and WSe2, where resistance switching occurs via in-plane anion migration or localized phase transitions [3-5].
